steps.title: Graph browser
steps.caption: The main browser opens a local neighborhood. Select nodes to inspect their connections; dragging, pinning and neighborhood controls use the same graph model.

steps.title: Reveal the complete graph
steps.caption: Show whole graph reveals stored nodes beyond the current neighborhood. Expansion, collapse and hiding change the visible graph while retaining the complete graph for editing and export.

steps.title: Graph spacing, canvas zoom and viewing lens
steps.caption: Graph spacing changes node distances. Canvas zoom scales shapes, labels and strokes together. The focus + context slider applies the independent nonlinear viewing lens.

steps.title: User key map
steps.caption: The help dialog and docs/KEYMAP.md share the same implemented command definitions, including graph spacing, canvas zoom, navigation, editing and file shortcuts.

steps.title: Node types and curved relations
steps.caption: The palette page shows all 21 configured Freshmind node types, labeled curved relations, parallel edges and a self-loop. Its YAML editor applies semantic and visual configuration to the existing graph.

steps.title: Open the approved Berry example
steps.caption: Berry is one of the two approved migrated datasets. The native YAML graph retains 21 nodes and 22 relations, annotations and original linked-resource paths.

steps.title: Florentine families
steps.caption: This public example has 15 families and 20 undirected marriage links. Node content contains graph-derived summaries and links to the connected families, with source attribution retained in the document.

steps.title: Edit a multiline node label
steps.caption: F2 opens an inline label editor on the selected node. A draft stays separate from the model until committed; node identity, relations and annotations are retained.

steps.title: Annotations and item details
steps.caption: Ctrl+Enter commits the label. Space or Show details opens the selected node's content in a separate, resizable popup. Internal links navigate to connected nodes; Edit content delegates to the annotation inspector.

steps.title: Save the complete graph as YAML
steps.caption: Ctrl+Shift+S opens the filename dialog. Saving downloads the complete stored graph, including hidden nodes, with optional layout/view state and embedded or companion type configuration.

steps.title: Single-focus comparison: ordinary layout
steps.caption: The synthetic crowded-star fixture uses a fixed center and fixed context anchors. This is the ordinary TouchGraph layout after 250 batches from the saved initial coordinates; RFC is off. Both comparison views use 200% graph spacing and 100% canvas zoom for readability.

steps.title: Single-focus comparison: reinforcement enabled
steps.caption: Reload the identical initial graph, activate RFC and run the same 250 batches. Strengthened focal springs and angular forces spread the branches more evenly; the 9 semantic nodes and 12 relations are unchanged. This comparison uses ordinary coordinate weights (1, 1). Focal-region exclusion remains later work.

steps.title: Weighted RFC for horizontally extended labels
steps.caption: The wide-label fixture uses horizontal coordinate weight 0.25 and vertical weight 1. Equal angles are measured in weighted physical coordinates, permitting a wider focal layout while the viewing lens and both zooms stay independent. Ordinary context springs still compete with reinforcement; the metric alone does not guarantee clear space or eliminate label overlaps.

steps.title: Browse the approved NIPS dataset
steps.caption: NIPS-FM contains 3,777 nodes and 5,257 relations. Opening it starts with a bounded neighborhood; the full graph remains stored for subsequent navigation and export.
